issues.description: Field mismatch: de.tum.in.ase.eist.model.Person#birthday. The problem statement UML and the template common model declare Person.birthday as java.time.LocalDate (used by the client UI DatePicker). The solution repository's common Person class, however, declares birthday as java.lang.String. Meanwhile the client code (PersonScene) expects and uses LocalDate (DatePicker.setValue(person.getBirthday())). This inconsistency will cause compilation type errors and runtime JSON (de)serialization confusion for students trying to run or implement the exercise.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent type for Person.birthday across all artifacts. Prefer java.time.LocalDate (as shown in the problem statement and template) so the client DatePicker and server-side logic align. Update the solution's common Person class to declare 'private LocalDate birthday;' and adjust any code that treated it as String. Ensure JSON serialization supports LocalDate (e.g., register Jackson JavaTimeModule on the server) so REST requests/responses work correctly.
